title: dedicated-fleet-autoscaler: add burst token-bucket, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Improved dedicated fleet autoscaler: introduces burst token-bucket controls, per-fleet throughput guarantees, and richer utilization reporting. Backwards-compatible config migration. Improves short-term tail latency and SLO compliance for bursty workloads.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets observed recurring tail latency and dropped requests during short bursty traffic patterns (customer reports + internal canaries). Existing autoscaler reacts slowly to sub-minute spikes; operators need configurable burst capacity allowances and clear throughput guarantees per fleet. This PR introduces a token-bucket based burst controller integrated with the fleet autoscaler, explicit per-fleet throughput_guarantee settings, and expanded utilization reporting for accurate billing and capacity planning.

What changed: added a new burst controller (token-bucket) that allows short-lived bursts up to a configurable token budget; integrated burst tokens into scheduling decisions so requests can be routed to burst capacity without violating longer-term SLOs; added throughput_guarantee and burst_budget config fields on FleetSpec; extended fleet metrics exporter to emit "fleet.burst_tokens", "fleet.throughput_effective_rps", and "fleet.utilization_5m/1h"; updated the UI route in Console to show burst and guarantee usage.

Migration: existing FleetSpec will default to burst disabled to preserve behavior. Admins can enable by adding throughput_guarantee (rps) and burst_budget (tokens) to their fleet definitions. We include a migration script (scripts/migrate_fleet_configs.py) that can annotate fleets with recommended defaults based on historical utilization.

Testing: unit tests for token-bucket logic and autoscaler decisioning added; integration test in perf-canary simulates bursty traffic, validates no drop in 99th latency while increasing effective throughput by ~22% during bursts; e2e test validates metrics emitted and Console UI panel renders. CI: build -> unit -> integration -> e2e -> perf.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4821)
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration/perf canary
- [x] Migration script and docs
- [x] Console UI changes gated behind feature flag

Related: follows up on previous autoscaler tuning work in ENG-3950 and addresses customer report SUP-903.

checks_summary: CI: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration (pass), e2e (pass), perf-canary (pass, 5 runs), lint (pass). One flaky test (pkg/autoscaler TestScaleDownRace) was quarantined and rerun; flake did not affect this PR.
performance_results: Perf canary (production-like fleet): +22% effective throughput during 30s bursts, 30s to recover token budget at default settings, 99th latency improved by 14% compared to baseline autoscaler under same load. CPU/GPU utilization averaged +8% during bursts, with no increased error rate.
notes: Console changes behind feature flag 'fleet_burst_ui'. Recommend rolling deploy to Dedicated control planes and run migrate_fleet_configs.py in dry-run first. Operations: monitor fleet.burst_tokens and tokens_dropped for first 48h post-rollout.
